motive: Enzo skimmed $40,000 from the family and sent it to the rival Calabrese family. The Don found the ledger and planned to expose him.
opportunity: Gino left the whiskey tray unattended in the hallway from 8:55 to 9:05. Enzo was in the hallway at 9:00 and near the study at 9:15.
method: Poison in the whiskey decanter on the unattended tray.
verdictNarration: It was Enzo Bellini. For twenty years he stood at the Don's right hand, and for the last two he had been bleeding the family dry, forty thousand dollars sent to the Calabreses. When the Don found the ledger, Enzo knew he had one night. At nine o'clock, while Gino stepped out for a smoke, Enzo poisoned the decanter on the unattended tray. He claimed he was smoking a cigar in the garden. But the garden snow was untouched, and Lucia had seen him in the study corridor at a quarter past nine. The snow kept his secret. It just couldn't lie for him.

timeline.event: Sal argues with the Don about gambling debts; Rosa overhears through the door.
Gino prepares the whiskey tray and leaves a note.
Gino leaves the tray in the hallway and steps out for a smoke.
Enzo poisons the decanter on the unattended whiskey tray.
Gino returns and sees Enzo walking away from the tray; he carries it to the study.
Enzo walks toward the study; Lucia sees him from the office door.
The Don drinks the poisoned whiskey.

clues.name: Torn ledger page
clues.text: A charred ledger page in the fireplace. One line survived: "$40,000 to C.F." in a careful hand.

clues.name: Telephone notepad
clues.text: By the telephone, in a woman's handwriting: "Bassi. Wills & Estates. Tomorrow, 10 am. Do NOT tell V."

clues.name: Engraved cufflink
clues.text: A gold cufflink engraved "E.B." under the Don's desk.

clues.name: Bitter decanter
clues.text: The crystal whiskey decanter. A bitter, almond-like residue clings to the bottom.

clues.name: Butler's note
clues.text: A note pinned by the stove: "Whiskey tray ready 8:50. G." But the tray only reached the study after nine.

clues.name: Untouched snow
clues.text: The garden snow is perfectly smooth, from the porch steps to the far wall. It stopped snowing at 8:45. No one walked here tonight.

enzo.personality: Smooth and loyal-sounding; answers questions with questions when pressed; never raises his voice.
enzo.deflection: Detective, I have answered that as plainly as a man can. Ask me something worth my time.

facts.text: I am the Don's consigliere. Twenty years at his side, through every war.

facts.truth: I was in the hallway at 9:00 and near the study at 9:15.
facts.lie_text: I was in the garden having a cigar from nine until I heard the screams.
facts.lie_text_v2: I stood under the porch by the garden door with my cigar. I never stepped into the snow.

facts.unlocked_text: Fine. I moved some money for the Calabreses. Business. But I did not kill him.

facts.text: I heard Sal and the Don screaming about money at half past eight. Sal owes everyone in Brooklyn.

facts.unlocked_text: Yes, that cufflink is mine. I am in that study every day of my life. It proves nothing.

facts.text: Only Gino serves the Don's whiskey. He is very particular about that tray.

sal.personality: Hot-headed, defensive, self-pitying; lashes out, then sulks.
sal.innocentSecretReveal: Sal Moretti did argue with his brother at half past eight, and he does owe the bookies. Eight hundred dollars, not forty thousand. After the fight he drank alone in the library until the screaming started. A fool and a debtor. Not a killer.
sal.deflection: Hey, I don't gotta answer that. Ask somebody else, pal.

facts.text: Vincent was my big brother. He never once let me forget it.

facts.truth: I was in the study arguing with Vincent at 8:30.
facts.lie_text: Half past eight? I was in the kitchen lookin' for a sandwich. Didn't see Vincent all night.
facts.lie_text_v2: Okay, maybe I stopped by the study for a minute around eight thirty. We talked. Brothers talk.

facts.text: From nine on I was in the library with a bottle, till I heard Rosa scream.

facts.unlocked_text: Forty grand? You think that's me? I owe the bookies eight hundred, tops. I couldn't lose forty grand if I tried.

facts.text: Enzo's been strange for weeks. New suits, new car, and always on that telephone.

rosa.personality: Composed, cutting, protective of her dignity; answers with understatement.
rosa.innocentSecretReveal: Rosa Moretti was planning to leave her husband. She had an appointment with Arturo Bassi, a lawyer for wills and estates, and she listened at the study door to hear what Vincent said about the will. She wanted his money, not his death.
rosa.deflection: I don't believe that is any of your concern, detective.

facts.text: Twenty-two years married to Vincent. Long enough to know every one of his lies.
At half past eight I heard Sal shouting at Vincent in the study. About money, as always.

facts.truth: I was outside the study door at 8:30 and on the telephone in the library around 9:00.
facts.lie_text: I was upstairs in my room all evening, until I came down and found him.
facts.lie_text_v2: I was upstairs most of the evening. I may have come down once for a book.

facts.unlocked_text: Yes, I telephoned a lawyer. I intended to leave Vincent and take what I was owed. A divorce, detective, not a funeral.

facts.text: I found him at half past nine. The decanter was on the desk; Gino always brings it at nine sharp. Tonight it was late.

lucia.personality: Timid, precise with numbers, frightened; apologizes often and avoids naming names.
lucia.innocentSecretReveal: Lucia Ferraro was frightened, not guilty. She had seen Enzo Bellini in the study corridor at a quarter past nine, and she had known for months that his figures didn't balance. She kept quiet because she was afraid of him.
lucia.deflection: I... I'm sorry, detective. I'd really rather not say.

facts.text: I keep the family's books. Six years now. The Don was always fair to me.
I was in the bookkeeping office off the study corridor all evening, going over the accounts.

facts.unlocked_text: All right. At a quarter past nine I saw Mr. Bellini in the study corridor, heading toward the Don's door. Please, he can't know I told you.
That's Mr. Bellini's handwriting. C.F.... the Calabrese Family. The books haven't balanced in months. I was too scared to tell the Don.

facts.text: Some men in this house frighten me, detective. I'd rather not say which.

gino.personality: Dutiful, laconic, ashamed of any failure; addresses everyone formally.
gino.innocentSecretReveal: Gino Russo left the whiskey tray unattended in the hallway for ten minutes while he stepped out for a smoke. He has carried that shame all night. When he came back, he saw Mr. Bellini walking away from the tray.
gino.deflection: With respect, sir, I only serve. I don't gossip.

facts.text: Fifteen years I have driven and served the Don, sir. He was a good master.
I prepared the whiskey tray at ten minutes to nine, as every night, and carried it to the study myself.

facts.truth: I stepped out the kitchen back door for a smoke from 8:55 to 9:05.
facts.lie_text: I was in the kitchen the whole time, sir, polishing the silver.
facts.lie_text_v2: I was in the kitchen, sir. Perhaps I stepped to the back door for a breath of air.

facts.unlocked_text: Forgive me, sir. I left the tray in the hallway and stepped out for a smoke. Ten minutes. When I came back, Mr. Bellini was walking away from it.

facts.text: It is not my place to accuse anyone, sir. But the family has been quarrelling over money for weeks.
